messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: "Flipping" the frequency spectrum
parts:
Hi Julia,

I think your best bet is to use a combo of layout() and plotting the frequency spectrum by hand. If you check out a conversation Martin and I had a couple of weeks ago, we go over how to extract spectrum data and plot it by hand (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/seewave/_69Stm_gTtc).

You can then use plot(x = , y = , etc.) to plot the axes as you want them. I would play around with the layout() function to group the three plots together (http://www.statmethods.net/advgraphs/layout.html).

If you're comfortable with R, there are also ways of extracting data from all three of the plots and plotting them with ggplot2 and grid.arrange. However, spectrograms in ggplot2 can be extremely computationally challenging in my experience! I usually have to downsample them first.

Good luck and let us know how it goes,

Steffi

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: "Flipping" the frequency spectrum
parts:
Hello Julia,

Here is a solution. The trick is to set plot=2 in either meanspec() or spec()
HTH
Jerome

data(tico)
layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,0), nc=2, byrow=TRUE),width=c(2,1), height=c(3,1))
par(mar=c(0,4.5,1,0))
spectro(tico, scale=FALSE, tlab="", axisX=FALSE, yaxt="n", cex.lab=1.2)
par(mar=c(0,0,1,1))
meanspec(tico, plot=2, flab="")
par(mar=c(4.5,4.5,0, 0))
oscillo(tico, bty="o")
